sanskrit: vṛṣā te 'haṃ vṛṣaṇyantyai garbhaṃ dadhāmi yonyām | yadi devapariṣṭhitā prajāṃ tokaṃ na vindase ||
english: I, the potent one, place an embryo in your womb for one who craves a bull-like male offspring; if, sustained by the gods, you do not obtain progeny nor a child.

sanskrit: dhātā te taṃ sinīvālī varuṇānī pra yacchatu | pumāṃsaṃ putram indrāṇī śatadāyaṃ dadhātu te ||
english: May Dhātṛ grant you that; may Sinīvālī, may Varuṇānī bestow it; may Indrāṇī place in you a male son, one who bestows a hundredfold.

sanskrit: saṃvṛtas te vakṣaṇāsu garbhaḥ puṃsā pumān kṛtaḥ | sarvāṅgas tanvor jāyatām agnir ivāraṇyor adhi ||
english: The embryo enclosed within your flanks has been fashioned as a male by a male; may he be born complete in all limbs, as fire arises from the two araṇī fire-sticks.

sanskrit: dhatsva vīraṃ karmaṇyaṃ prasvaṃ tvāvadhrim avaśāṃ kṛṇomi | ātmanas te lohitād garbhaḥ saṃvartatāṃ vṛṣā ||
english: Bear a heroic, capable son; I make of you a good breeder, I render the unmated one subject. From your own blood let a potent embryo be formed.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā piṃśatu te prajāṃ dhātā tokaṃ dadhātu te | rākā sīvyatu sūcyā bhūtasyeśānā bhuvanasya devī ||
english: May Tvaṣṭṛ fashion your offspring; may Dhātṛ establish a child for you; may Rākā sew with her needle — she who is sovereign of what has come to be and of the world, the goddess.

sanskrit: sinīvālīm anumatiṃ rākāṃ guṅguṃ sarasvatīm | devānāṃ patnīr yā devīr indrāṇīm avase huve ||
english: Sinīvālī, Anumati, Rākā, Guṅgu, and Sarasvatī — the divine consorts of the gods, those goddesses — and Indrāṇī I invoke for protection.

sanskrit: abhinnāṇḍā vṛddhagarbhā- -ariṣṭā vīrasūr iyam | vi jāyatāṃ pra jāyatāṃ bahvī bhavatu putriṇī ||
english: Unbroken in the egg, with a fully grown embryo, unharmed, a bearer of heroes — may she give birth, may she bring forth abundantly; may she become one blessed with many sons.

sanskrit: pari sṛja garbhaṃ dhehi māśāḥ pra cyoṣṭa lohitam | anūnaḥ pūrṇo jāyatām aśrāmoranvo apiśācadhītaḥ ||
english: Release the embryo, place it — do not hold back, do not expel the blood; may the child be born undeficient, complete, unexhausted, uninjured, uncontaminated by Piśācas.

sanskrit: tvaṃ dadhāsi dvipade catuṣpade garbhaṃ prajām ejate viśvarūpām | kanikradad vṛṣabho vīḍuśepāḥ prajāpate tanvāṃ dhehi garbham ||
english: You sustain the embryo and the offspring of every form for the biped and the quadruped as they quicken; O Prajāpati, bull that roars and bears a mighty member, place the embryo in the bodies.

sanskrit: abhikrandaṃ stanayaṃ dhehi garbhaṃ vidyotamānaḥ pavamāno vīrudbhiḥ | parjanyemāṃ pṛthivī retasāvata- -apāṃ rasair oṣadhīnāṃ paśūnām ||
english: Roaring forth with his thunder, flashing, the purifying wind places the embryo with the plants; may Parjanya water this earth with seed, with the essences of waters, of plants, of cattle.

sanskrit: ā te nayāmi vṛṣaṇaṃ yaḥ prajānāṃ prajāpatiḥ | sa te dadhātv ṛtviyaṃ garbhaṃ yonyāṃ vijāṃ prajām ||
english: I lead to you the potent one who is Prajāpati of creatures; may he place in your womb the embryo in its due season, the offspring of noble birth.

sanskrit: ye vṛṣāṇo garbhakṛta ṛtviyānāṃ samenasaḥ | tāṃs te hvayāmi tad u te sam ṛdhyatām ||
english: Those potent ones who are creators of the embryo among those who come at the right season, guilt-sharing — those I summon for you; and may that prosper and be fulfilled for you.

sanskrit: agneṣ ṭe tvaṣṭur varuṇād indrāt somād bṛhaspateḥ | putraṃ te putrakāmāyai devebhyo nir mame prajām ||
english: From Agni, from Tvaṣṭṛ, from Varuṇa, from Indra, from Soma, from Bṛhaspati — for you who desire a son, I fashion offspring from the gods.

sanskrit: aṅgād aṅgāt saṃ sravatu tad yonau prati tiṣṭhatu | prajā te vakṣaṇāśayā tat te bījaṃ vi rohatu ||
english: May it flow together from limb to limb; may it find its place in the womb; the offspring that lies in your flanks — may that seed of yours sprout forth.

sanskrit: atsaso yamanaṃ saso 'bhūtir yakṣmam ajījanat | imaṃ sahasrabhāg indro viśaraṃ nāśayāti te ||
english: From overeating, from indigestion, from distress, from failure — these engendered the disease viśara; this Indra, who has a thousandfold share, destroys the viśara for you.

sanskrit: yaḥ kāryo yaś ca kṛtaḥ svayaṃjā uta hāryaḥ | devā indrajyeṣṭhā viśaraṃ nāśayantu te ||
english: That which is to be done, and that which has been done, that which is self-born, and that which is stolen — may the gods with Indra as chief destroy the viśara for you.

sanskrit: viśarasya vijṛmbhasya- -iṣur mātā dhanuṣ pitā | ādityāḥ putrā ādityā viśaraṃ naśayantu te ||
english: The arrow is the mother of viśara and its spreading; the bow is the father; the Ādityas are the sons — may the Ādityas destroy the viśara for you.

sanskrit: dhanvano jyāyā iṣvā apaskambhasya bāhvoḥ | apāṣṭhāc chṛṅgāt kurmalād viśaraṃ nāśayāmi te ||
english: From the bowstring of the bow, from the arrow, from the arms of the prop; from the iron, from the horn, from the kurmalā — I destroy the viśara for you.

sanskrit: alavatī ruruśīrṣṇy atho yasyāyo mukham | devyai parjanyaretasa iṣave kṛṇutā namaḥ ||
english: The alavatī with its ruru-skull head, and that arrow whose face is iron — to the divine arrow begotten of Parjanya's seed, make obeisance.

sanskrit: yām atrayo aṅgiraso gotamā vīrudhaṃ viduḥ | tayā bharadvājaḥ kaṇvo viśaraṃ nāśayāti te ||
english: The herb that the Atris, the Āṅgirasas, and the Gotamas have known — with that herb Bharadvāja and Kaṇva destroy the viśara for you.

sanskrit: yas tvā straiṇād apasaro yaḥ puṃso adhyāruhat | āklāntaṃ saṃklāntaṃ snāva tad u te kalpayāmasi ||
english: That which has spread from a woman's wound, that which has mounted over a man — the sinew weakened and afflicted together, that too we set right for you.

sanskrit: vāta ivābhraṃ cyāvayāmi yakṣmaṃ te tanvas pari | vācā yac cakrus te guru tad ṛcā laghu kṛṇmasi | tenāham ṛtodyena viśaraṃ nāśayāmi te ||
english: As the wind drives away a cloud, I drive away the disease from your body all around; what they have made heavy upon you by speech, that we make light by the sacred verse; with this truth-utterance I destroy the viśara for you.

sanskrit: yathā na satyaṃ puruṣaḥ sadā vaditum arhati | viṣkandhaṃ tvad apaśaraṃ viśaraṃ puṣṭyāmayam | jambhaṃ hanugrābhaṃ śaṅkhaṃ tān ajenā ajāmasi ||
english: As a man is not always able to speak the truth — so too: the viṣkandha, the viśara that has gone away from you, the disease of wasting, the jambha, the hanugrābha, the śaṅkha — all these we drive away with the she-goat driven forth.

sanskrit: śunam id va oṣadhayo vi dadhe bheṣajāya kam | dhanāyuvaḥ sanāyuvaḥ puruṣaṃ pārayiṣṇavaḥ ||
english: For the good of you all do I distribute the herbs for healing; those that are bringers of wealth, bringers of lasting life, able to carry a man across to safety.

sanskrit: ātmatrāṇi devajūtā vīrudhāyuṣyā kṛtā | tayāham indradattayā viśaraṃ nāśayāmi te ||
english: Self-protecting, impelled by the gods, the herb made for long life — with that one, given by Indra, I destroy the viśara for you.

sanskrit: alasya vyañjanasya veṣṭanasyota parṇadheḥ | granther jyāyā iṣvā viśaraṃ nāśayāmi te ||
english: From the lazy one, from the condiment, from the wrapping, and from the leaf-holder; from the knot, from the bowstring, from the arrow — I destroy the viśara for you.

sanskrit: sākaṃ viṣkandha pra pata cāṣeṇa kikidīvyā | sākaṃ vātasya dhrājyā saha naśya nihākayā ||
english: Fly away together, O viṣkandha, along with the bluejay and the kikidīvī bird; perish together with the rushing of the wind, together with the nihākā.

sanskrit: jaṅgiḍo 'si jaṅgiḍo rakṣitāsi jaṅgiḍaḥ | dvipāc catuṣpād asmākaṃ sarvaṃ rakṣatu jaṅgiḍaḥ ||
english: You are jaṅgiḍa; you are the protector, jaṅgiḍa; may jaṅgiḍa protect all that is ours — biped and quadruped.

sanskrit: yā gṛtsyas tripañcāśīḥ śataṃ kṛtyākṛtaś ca ye | sarvān vinaktatejaso 'rasān jaṅgiḍas karat ||
english: The gṛtyas fifty-three in number, and the hundred who have fabricated kṛtyas — all of them jaṅgiḍa has made devoid of power and shorn of potency.

sanskrit: arasaṃ kṛtrimaṃ nāḍam arasāḥ sapta visrasaḥ | apeto jaṅgiḍāmatim iṣum asteva sādhaya ||
english: The powerless artificial reed, the seven powerless visrasas — drive away the hostility of jaṅgiḍa's adversary as one dispatches an arrow.

sanskrit: kṛtyādūṣaṇa evāyam atho arātidūṣaṇaḥ | atho sahasvāṃ jaṅgiḍaḥ pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ||
english: He is the destroyer of kṛtyā-sorcery; he is the destroyer of enmity as well; and mighty jaṅgiḍa shall carry our lives across to safety.

sanskrit: sa jaṅgiḍasya mahimā pari ṇaḥ pātu viśvataḥ | viṣkandhaṃ yena sāsāha saṃskandham oja ojasā ||
english: May that greatness of jaṅgiḍa protect us on all sides — he by whose might he has overpowered the viṣkandha and the saṃskanda with force upon force.

sanskrit: tṛṣṭvā devā ajanayan niṣṭhitaṃ bhūmyām adhi | tam u tvāṅgirā iti brahmāṇaḥ pūrvyā viduḥ ||
english: Having sought him eagerly, the gods generated him established upon the earth; him the ancient brahmin seers of the Āṅgirasa lineage too have known as such.

sanskrit: na tvā pūrvā oṣadhayo na tvā tarantu yā navāḥ | vibādha ugro jaṅgiḍaḥ paripāṇaḥ sumaṅgalaḥ ||
english: Let neither the older herbs surpass you, nor those that are new; thrust-aside-all, fierce jaṅgiḍa, all-protecting, most auspicious.

sanskrit: aśvopadān bhagavo jaṅgiḍāmitavīrya | purā ta ugrāya sata upendro vīryaṃ dadau ||
english: O revered jaṅgiḍa of immeasurable virility, with horse's hoof-prints — formerly, when you were fierce, Upendra gave you your virility.

sanskrit: ugra it te vanaspata indra ojmānam ā dadhau | amīvāḥ sarvāś cātayañ jahi rakṣāṃsy oṣadhe ||
english: Indeed, Indra placed fierce power in you, O lord of the forest; scattering all diseases, strike down the rākṣasas, O herb.

sanskrit: aśarīkaṃ viśarīkaṃ balāsaṃ puṣṭyāmayam | takmānaṃ viśvaśāradam arasaṃ jaṅgiḍas karat ||
english: Aśarīka, viśarīka, balāsa, the disease of wasting, the takman that recurs each autumn — all these jaṅgiḍa has made powerless.
